nodes.outcome: State Euclid's first axiom that things which are equal to the same thing are equal to one another, and apply it to justify a simple equality

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Axioms: add/subtract equals
nodes.outcome: Apply the axioms about adding equals to equals and subtracting equals from equals to justify statements such as if x = y then x + 3 = y + 3

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Whole and part axioms
nodes.outcome: State the axioms that the whole is greater than the part, and apply them to reject claims like half of a segment exceeding the whole

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Coincidence axiom
nodes.outcome: Apply the axiom that things which coincide with one another are equal to conclude two segments are equal by superposition

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Justify via axioms
nodes.outcome: Justify a multi-step statement such as if AB = PQ and PQ = CD then AB = CD by naming the axiom used at each step

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Axioms need no proof
nodes.outcome: Explain why axioms are accepted without proof as self-evident universal truths on which all deductions rest

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Postulates 1–3 stated
nodes.outcome: State Euclid's first three postulates: drawing a straight line through any two points, extending it indefinitely, and drawing a circle with any centre and radius

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Unique line through points
nodes.outcome: Illustrate with a drawing that exactly one straight line can be drawn through two distinct points

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Extending a segment
nodes.outcome: Draw a finite straight segment extended further in either direction, matching the second postulate

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Drawing circles
nodes.outcome: Given a marked centre and a radius, draw the circle described by the third postulate and identify centre and radius on the figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Fourth postulate
nodes.outcome: State the fourth postulate that all right angles are equal to one another and mark equal right angles on a figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Fifth postulate stated
nodes.outcome: State Euclid's fifth postulate about two lines cut by a transversal meeting where the sum of inner angles is less than two right angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Draw fifth postulate figure
nodes.outcome: Draw the transversal figure of the fifth postulate, marking interior angles whose sum is less than 180° and the side on which the lines meet

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Predict side of intersection
nodes.outcome: Given a figure with a transversal, predict on which side the two lines will meet according to the fifth postulate

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Compare angle sums
nodes.outcome: For several transversal figures, decide whether the sum of interior angles equals, exceeds, or falls short of two right angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Why postulate five differs
nodes.outcome: Compare the short first four postulates with the long fifth postulate and explain why Euclid avoided using it until late in the Elements

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Postponed use
nodes.outcome: Identify that Euclid proved his early results without the fifth postulate, treating it as possibly unnecessary

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Failed proof attempts
nodes.outcome: Explain why centuries of attempts to deduce the fifth postulate from the others failed, leading to equivalent versions instead

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Playfair's axiom
nodes.outcome: State Playfair's axiom: for every line and point not on it, exactly one parallel line passes through the point

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Draw Playfair figure
nodes.outcome: Draw a line, an external point and the unique parallel through it, then attempt a second parallel and explain why none exists

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Equivalence sketch
nodes.outcome: Explain in words why Playfair's version implies Euclid's fifth postulate and vice versa, so assuming either gives the same geometry

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Two lines through point
nodes.outcome: Show that two lines cannot both pass through a single point and be parallel to the same third line, using Playfair's uniqueness

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Angle sum version
nodes.outcome: State the equivalent condition that two lines are parallel when the sum of co-interior angles with a transversal is exactly two right angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Parallel lines meaning
nodes.outcome: Define non-intersecting (parallel) lines as lines in the same plane that never meet however far they are produced

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Constant distance test
nodes.outcome: Verify whether two drawn lines stay equidistant at three chosen places and relate constant distance to being non-intersecting

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Consistency of assumptions
nodes.outcome: Explain that a system of axioms must be consistent, so no theorem may contradict another or an axiom

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Independence of axioms
nodes.outcome: Explain what it means for an axiom to be independent — not deducible from the others — and connect this to the status of the fifth postulate

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Deductive reasoning
nodes.outcome: Contrast deductive reasoning, which derives conclusions from accepted truths, with empirical verification by measuring drawings

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Theorem and proof
nodes.outcome: Identify the parts of a mathematical argument — given, to prove, construction, proof — as used in the Elements

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Euclid's Elements
nodes.outcome: Describe the Elements as thirteen books organising all known geometry from a handful of definitions, axioms and postulates

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Lines have no ends
nodes.outcome: Recognise that treating lines as endless is an idealisation assumed in the postulates, not something a drawing can show fully

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Flat plane assumption
nodes.outcome: State that Euclidean geometry assumes all figures lie in a flat plane, and identify figures drawn on curved surfaces as outside this assumption

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Beyond the fifth postulate
nodes.outcome: Give a qualitative example (triangles on a sphere) showing geometry changes if the fifth postulate is replaced

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Axiom word application
nodes.outcome: Solve a comparison problem such as 'Ravi and Farida have equal marbles; Ravi gains some' by naming which axiom guarantees the conclusion

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Assumption or result?
nodes.outcome: Classify given sentences as definition, axiom, postulate or provable result within Euclid's framework

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Recall proof method
nodes.outcome: Recall that geometry results are proved from previously proved facts and axioms

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Name basic objects
nodes.outcome: Name the basic objects used in geometry: line, ray, and angle

nodes.title: Define ray
nodes.outcome: Define a ray as a part of a line with one endpoint and extending infinitely in one direction

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define angle
nodes.outcome: Define an angle as the figure formed by two rays with a common endpoint

nodes.title: Define acute angle
nodes.outcome: Define an acute angle and give an example with its measure between 0° and 90°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define right angle
nodes.outcome: Define a right angle and give an example with measure exactly 90°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define obtuse angle
nodes.outcome: Define an obtuse angle and give an example with its measure between 90° and 180°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define straight angle
nodes.outcome: Define a straight angle and give an example with measure exactly 180°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define reflex angle
nodes.outcome: Define a reflex angle and give an example with its measure between 180° and 360°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Classify angle by measure
nodes.outcome: Classify an angle as acute, right, obtuse, straight, or reflex given its degree measure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify adjacent angles
nodes.outcome: Identify adjacent angles in a figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify linear pair
nodes.outcome: Identify a linear pair of adjacent angles in a figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify vertically opposite angles
nodes.outcome: Identify vertically opposite angles formed by intersecting lines

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define complementary angles
nodes.outcome: Define complementary angles as two angles whose sum is 90°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define supplementary angles
nodes.outcome: Define supplementary angles as two angles whose sum is 180°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify complementary pairs
nodes.outcome: Identify whether a pair of angles are complementary

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify supplementary pairs
nodes.outcome: Identify whether a pair of angles are supplementary

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Explain intersecting lines
nodes.outcome: Explain that two lines in a plane intersect if they have exactly one common point

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Explain parallel lines
nodes.outcome: Explain that two lines in a plane are parallel if they never meet

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Parallel lines constant distance
nodes.outcome: Relate parallel lines to the property that the distance between them is constant

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Use linear pair property
nodes.outcome: Use the linear pair property to find unknown angles in a figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State vertically opposite equal
nodes.outcome: State that vertically opposite angles are equal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove vertically opposite equal
nodes.outcome: Prove that vertically opposite angles are equal using the linear pair axiom

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply vertically opposite equality
nodes.outcome: Apply the equality of vertically opposite angles to find unknown angles in a figure

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Solve comp/supp multi-step
nodes.outcome: Solve multi-step problems involving complementary and supplementary angle relations

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define transversal
nodes.outcome: Define a transversal as a line that intersects two or more lines at distinct points

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify corresponding angles
nodes.outcome: Identify corresponding angles formed by a transversal cutting two lines

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify alternate interior angles
nodes.outcome: Identify alternate interior angles formed by a transversal cutting two lines

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify alternate exterior angles
nodes.outcome: Identify alternate exterior angles formed by a transversal cutting two lines

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify co-interior angles
nodes.outcome: Identify co-interior (same-side interior) angles formed by a transversal cutting two lines

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State corresponding angles axiom
nodes.outcome: State that if two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, then each pair of corresponding angles is equal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State alternate interior theorem
nodes.outcome: State the theorem: alternate interior angles are equal when parallel lines are cut by a transversal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State alternate exterior theorem
nodes.outcome: State the theorem: alternate exterior angles are equal when parallel lines are cut by a transversal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State co-interior theorem
nodes.outcome: State that co-interior (same-side interior) angles are supplementary when parallel lines are cut by a transversal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply corresponding angles
nodes.outcome: Use the corresponding angles axiom to find unknown angles when parallel lines are cut by a transversal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply alternate interior angles
nodes.outcome: Use the alternate interior angles theorem to find unknown angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply alternate exterior angles
nodes.outcome: Use the alternate exterior angles theorem to find unknown angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply co-interior angles
nodes.outcome: Use the co-interior angles theorem to find unknown angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Converse corresponding angles
nodes.outcome: Use the converse of the corresponding angles axiom to conclude that two lines are parallel

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Converse alternate interior angles
nodes.outcome: Use the converse of the alternate interior angles theorem to conclude that two lines are parallel

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Converse co-interior angles
nodes.outcome: Use the converse of the co-interior angles theorem to conclude that two lines are parallel

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Combined parallel line problems
nodes.outcome: Solve for unknown angles in figures involving parallel lines cut by a transversal using multiple angle relations

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State angle sum of triangle
nodes.outcome: State that the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove angle sum of triangle
nodes.outcome: Prove that the sum of the angles of a triangle is 180° using parallel lines and transversal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply angle sum of triangle
nodes.outcome: Apply the angle sum property to find missing angles in a triangle

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State exterior angle theorem
nodes.outcome: State the exterior angle theorem: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove exterior angle theorem
nodes.outcome: Prove the exterior angle theorem using the angle sum property

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply exterior angle theorem
nodes.outcome: Apply the exterior angle theorem to find unknown angles in triangles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Solve combined triangle problems
nodes.outcome: Solve problems that combine the angle sum property and exterior angle theorem with parallel line relations

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define triangle
nodes.outcome: Define a triangle as a three-sided closed polygon

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Name triangle parts
nodes.outcome: Name the vertices, sides, and angles of a given triangle

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define scalene triangle
nodes.outcome: Define a scalene triangle as a triangle with all sides of different lengths

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define isosceles triangle
nodes.outcome: Define an isosceles triangle as a triangle with at least two equal sides

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define equilateral triangle
nodes.outcome: Define an equilateral triangle as a triangle with all sides equal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define acute triangle
nodes.outcome: Define an acute triangle as a triangle with all angles less than 90°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define right triangle
nodes.outcome: Define a right triangle as a triangle with one right angle

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Define obtuse triangle
nodes.outcome: Define an obtuse triangle as a triangle with one angle greater than 90°

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Classify by sides
nodes.outcome: Classify a given triangle as scalene, isosceles, or equilateral based on side lengths

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Classify by angles
nodes.outcome: Classify a given triangle as acute, right, or obtuse based on angle measures

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State congruence meaning
nodes.outcome: State that congruent figures have exactly the same shape and size

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Write vertex correspondence
nodes.outcome: Given two triangles, write a correspondence of vertices (e.g., A↔P, B↔Q, C↔R) such that the triangles could be congruent

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Use congruence notation
nodes.outcome: Use the symbol ≅ correctly in statements like ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR

nodes.title: Identify equal parts from congruence
nodes.outcome: Given a congruence statement ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, identify all equal corresponding sides and angles

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: List six equal parts
nodes.outcome: List all three pairs of equal sides and three pairs of equal angles from a given triangle congruence

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State SAS criterion
nodes.outcome: State the SAS congruence criterion: if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another triangle, the triangles are congruent

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State ASA criterion
nodes.outcome: State the ASA congruence criterion: if two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to two angles and the included side of another triangle, the triangles are congruent

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State SSS criterion
nodes.outcome: State the SSS congruence criterion: if three sides of one triangle are equal to three sides of another triangle, the triangles are congruent

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State RHS criterion
nodes.outcome: State the RHS congruence criterion: if the hypotenuse and one side of a right triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of another right triangle, the triangles are congruent

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify congruence criterion
nodes.outcome: Given two triangles with marked equal parts, identify which congruence criterion (SAS, ASA, SSS, RHS) applies or state that none applies

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply SAS criterion
nodes.outcome: Prove two triangles congruent using the SAS criterion given appropriate equalities in a diagram

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply ASA criterion
nodes.outcome: Prove two triangles congruent using the ASA criterion given appropriate equalities

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply SSS criterion
nodes.outcome: Prove two triangles congruent using the SSS criterion given appropriate equalities

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply RHS criterion
nodes.outcome: Prove two right triangles congruent using the RHS criterion

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Set up congruence proof
nodes.outcome: Given a geometric diagram, identify the triangles to prove congruent and write the given statements and what is to be proved

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Write two-column proof
nodes.outcome: Complete a two-column proof of triangle congruence by filling statements and reasons, including the congruence criterion and CPCTC

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Use CPCTC
nodes.outcome: State that corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal (CPCTC) and apply it to deduce equal sides or angles after proving congruence

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State angles opposite equal sides
nodes.outcome: State the theorem: angles opposite to equal sides of a triangle are equal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove angles opposite equal sides
nodes.outcome: Prove that angles opposite equal sides are equal using SAS congruence (drop median or bisector)

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply angles equal sides
nodes.outcome: Find unknown angles in an isosceles triangle using the property that angles opposite equal sides are equal, combined with angle sum

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State sides opposite equal angles
nodes.outcome: State the converse: sides opposite to equal angles of a triangle are equal

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove sides opposite equal angles
nodes.outcome: Prove that sides opposite equal angles are equal using congruence (e.g., drop perpendicular from vertex, use ASA or AAS)

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Apply sides equal angles
nodes.outcome: Find unknown side lengths in an isosceles triangle using the property that sides opposite equal angles are equal, combined with given side measures

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Identify isosceles triangle
nodes.outcome: Determine whether a triangle is isosceles given side lengths or angle measures using equal sides or equal angles property

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Combine isosceles and angle sum
nodes.outcome: Solve problems that combine isosceles triangle properties and angle sum property to find unknown angles in composite figures

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove altitude bisects base
nodes.outcome: Prove that in an isosceles triangle, the altitude from the vertex to the base bisects the base using congruence

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State greater side greater angle
nodes.outcome: State the theorem: in a triangle, the greater side has the greater angle opposite it

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Order angles from sides
nodes.outcome: Given the side lengths of a triangle, order the angles from smallest to largest using the greater-side-greater-angle theorem

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State greater angle greater side
nodes.outcome: State the converse: in a triangle, the greater angle has the greater side opposite it

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Order sides from angles
nodes.outcome: Given the angle measures of a triangle, order the sides from smallest to largest using the greater-angle-greater-side theorem

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: State triangle inequality
nodes.outcome: State the triangle inequality: the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle is greater than the length of the third side

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Verify triangle inequality
nodes.outcome: Given three lengths, check whether they satisfy the triangle inequality and determine if they can form a triangle

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Find third side range
nodes.outcome: Given two side lengths of a triangle, determine the range of possible lengths for the third side using the triangle inequality

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Solve inequality word problems
nodes.outcome: Solve word problems involving triangle inequalities, such as finding minimum or maximum perimeter given side constraints

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove greater side greater angle
nodes.outcome: Prove that in a triangle, if one side is longer than another, the angle opposite the longer side is larger

nodes.subject: Mathematics
nodes.title: Prove greater angle greater side
nodes.outcome: Prove the converse: in a triangle, if one angle is larger than another, the side opposite the larger angle is longer
